title: Program areas, at a glance
subject: The Areas tab of the Program view in the Web Tools app

brief.background: A program's charter divides its work into areas, and the Areas tab showed them as a spine of numbered nodes over cards a phone swiped through one at a time, each card the same four rows. The owner asked to see every area at once, without the sentence over the page, as a dashboard with an icon for each area, and with each area showing what it has rather than one template filled the same way.
brief.methodology: The eight concepts were sketched on the Sessions program's five areas before any was judged. Each had to show every area at once on a phone and a desktop, keep the commits of the last fortnight and the measure where one attaches, and say whether it lets two areas differ in what they show.

grafts: the fortnight of day cells at each tile's foot, so activity still compares across areas
one header and one footer on every tile, the scoreboard's shared columns kept where comparison needs them
an area that declares nothing still gets a tile with its header, measure and fortnight, so a missing panel shows as a plain tile
selection.rationale: The owner asked for every area at once, more overview, an icon for each area, and areas that differ in what they show while the whole stays one piece. The bento is the only concept that lets an area's insides follow its own material, a measure for Reply, a breakdown for Delivery, thumbnails for Pages, while the shared header and footer, and the program's colour used only for its icons and measures, keep the tiles comparable. Declaring the panels in the manifest keeps the choice of what each area shows as data a reader can change.
assumptions: Does a tile's width read as importance, when it only follows how much its panels draw?
Is a registry grouped by one column a fair picture of an area, or does it count what is easy to count?
Will the owner keep declaring panels as areas change, or should an undeclared area show more than its measure?
